I can be of most valuable aid in the successful exploration of the [[Outer Planes]]. If you have stolen me, please be aware that now, bounty hunters are coming to claim me for justice. : I perform only in the Outer Planes. My information comes straight from the mouths of [[planewalker]]s, [[proxy|proxies]], or [[petitioner]]s. I have been carried around the Outer Planes by agents who have sought out those who have had experience in various subjects. Inscribed on me are their voices and impressions. : '''(Various overlapping voices)''' : '''[[Ariana Arachnis]]''': There are sixteen [[gate-town]]s in the — : '''Various voices''': Why won't it stop whistling in my ears?! : '''[[Jeobi Groove]]''': If you're looking for more, there's plenty of inns — : '''[[Flatnose Grim]]''': Get out! : '''Various voices''': Lord [[Quentill Paracs|Paracs]] is the brains behind the— : '''Mimir''': And they will speak to you directly of their experiences, though they cannot answer questions. They are simply recordings, and the sights they see may or may not be true, or they may color the sights and sounds with their own perceptions. : I am yours to command. Speak to me, and I will tell you all I know. == Background Information == * Due to the overlapping voices that make up the mimir's voice, it's difficult to tell if the opening line is "I am mimir" or "I am a mir" -- it may have been intended to be "I am a mimir" but two syllables were inadvertently combined by the voices. * The voice samples come from, in order, Track 2: [[A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Gate-towns|Gate-towns]], Track 4: [[A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Bedlam|Bedlam]], Track 17: [[A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Tradegate|Tradegate]], Track 10: [[A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Glorium|Glorium]], and Track 13: [[A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Ribcage|Ribcage]]. == External Links == [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=O05Pr6b_CAw This track on YouTube] {| class="fandom-table browser" style="width:100%" | class="prev"|'''Previous Track'''

page.title: A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Plague-Mort

revision.text:
['''Mimir''']
The gate-town to the Abyss is called Plague-Mort. It is a collection of buildings loosely governed by a being called the Arch-Lector, with his group of secret police, the Hounds, enforcing his edicts. Speaking of Plague-Mort is Alexander Brisimain.
[Alexander Brisimain ]
I'm a member of the Hounds. Let's get that straight right off the mark, berk. And I won't crease your face for you!. I'm one of the watchmen for this here, berk. And I do my duty, see? Make sure that old Birry gets his sum and protection money. And that no leatherhead comes along and burns down the town! Which reminds me, it almost happened a wee while back. The Abyss decided that Plague-Mort 's time had come. And so they sent a bag of fiends up to collect it!. Well, a few berks can outfight a ta'nari. And besides, the fiends were offering a lot of power to a lot of people. Only a total berk could turn that down. So we went along with the fiends in their plan to bring chaos and evil to the town! I mean, it's not like the locals are all sweetness and light, right? We were told to wait until the signal, which turned out to be the death of Arch-Lector Birry Yarmoril! So we all got together and muscled around some of the weaker sods. And then it turns out the fiends are peeling us... cuz there's other groups of ants who want to loot the birds and they're led by a ta'nari too!
Well, the chaos started and the flames were spouting out of the buildings like blades of razor vine. So, we figured to profit from the chaos anyway. The gate to the abyss was getting bigger. But, but no one paid that any mind. Then, someone realizes... we're all going to wind up in the abyss! And so, we get the town together enough to keep the gate at bay.
So, the fiends are defeated, the town gets rebuilt, and the Arch-Lector comes back. What's the point of the whole thing? I ask. What a waste of time. All that mutiny for nothing. Hey, no one else is going to hear this, right? Huh?

page.title: A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Realm of the Norns

revision.text:
['''Mimir''']
Deep in the undergrowth, fairly near Faunel, there sits a Grove of trees. Inside the Grove lies The Well of Earth, a scrying pool controlled by the Norns, or the three Fates.
[He Ge]
Hi, my name is He Ge, and I'm from Bedlam. Or was it Pandemonium? Well, whatever. I'm the best sodding thief in Mimir-recording in the Outlands, and don't let anyone tell you otherwise. I like to talk but I can also put a lid on it man, you know? I'm not one to rattle on and on like some berks I know, but they still say I talk too much. It's not true. Anyway, I'm here in the realm of the Norns to take a look into the scrying pool. They said I should check this place out and I figured I might as well take a quick glimpse into what the future's got in store for me. All right. there's no Norns around. Little gray witches always scare me anyway for some reason. So that's just as well. Hmm, I'll look into the pool.
All right, there I am walking juntly into a dragon’s lair. I'm talking to something I'm holding but I can't see what... Hmmm, now all I see is a mouthful of teeth, like a dragon's. Then there's an hourglass, with all the sand run out... oh then just red, uh-oh. Does this mean I'm going to die? Well, if I'm going into a dragon lair, you can bet that I'm going to be a lot more careful than that. Boy, I really look stupid there. I think I'll have to change my wardrobe. Oh well, I can't understand this thing. It doesn't make any sense at all. Stupid fate pool. Well, I'm off to this place called the Mausoleum of Chronepsis- I'm going to be taking something from there for one of my clients. Maybe that'll be a little more exciting than this stupid pool.

page.title: A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Ribcage

revision.text:
['''Mimir''']
In the veil of the Spine, sandwiched between Torch and Rigus, is Ribcage, the gate-town to Baator, the pits of desolation and despair. The great pass nearby cuts through the veil of the spine, significantly shortening the distance between Rigus and Ribcag. The town is said to be the most blatantly political in the Outlands with the power of all sorts buying influence, and influence buying a lucrative life. Lord quental parents controls the city with five Senators underneath him who can overturn his vote. This is Senator Lauren Dilfar, a member of one of the five senatorial families. Though he appears to be nothing more than a blowhard, Dilfar is said to be one of the most dangerous men in the city.
[Senator Lauren Dilfar]
The way I see it, Ribcage is like a great big body: The gate to Baator is the heart of town, what keeps the town functioning. And lord Parox is the brains behind the whole operation. My family is the lungs, providing refreshing necessary air to the body. The other families are the other organs, each providing a valuable service in its own way, but none of them are as valuable as the lungs, heart, and head. The brain can tell the lungs to stop breathing, but that doesn't last for long, otherwise the brain doesn't get air, and it withers and dies. The heart doesn't command, but without it, none of the other organs could function. Speaking of the heart, I've heard it said that Rigus is looking to tear the heart out of this body politic. Those scummy military swine want to take over everything. Well, trust me, not going to happen, no sire, no matter what they do. We're well defended, and we've got some allies that can swing any kind of battle our way. I'm talking about the pack, we're about to seal with some of the good gate towns. The good gate towns will just be acting in their own interest, and they'll certainly want to resist the expansionism of Rigus won't they

page.title: A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Rigus

revision.text:
['''Mimir'''] The military order of Acheron imposes itself on the gate-town of Rigus, making this a permanent encampment for armies great and small. It is built on a hill more than a mile tall, with seven terrace rings dividing the mighty from the meek, the powerful from the powerless. The top of the hill is called the crown. And it's from here that the generals of Rigus command the rest of the citizenry. Captain Timeroth Ress.
[Captain Timoth]
Right, new here are you? From Sigil, eh? Well, listen to me carefully. Do as I say and you won't have any problems. Life down here is a lot different than in Sigil, mark my words. Our orderly rank system keeps the town running smooth, with the lower ranks instantly obeying anything a higher rank tells them. Let me show you: Trooper.
[Random Soldier]
Sir! Yes, sir!
[Captain Timoth]
Climb at top that brick wall and jump off.
[Random Soldier]
Sir! Yes, sir!
[Captain Timoth]
Now you, as a visitor, wear this plaque to let people know you don't know the dark of things here. Since you're marked as a visitor, you don't have to do everything someone higher than you says (screams from a random soldier). You can claim the privilege of professional ignorance, see? But don't do it on purpose or you'll find the plaque stripped from you and there won't be a sodding thing you can do about it, right? Outstanding, trooper. Stand at ease.
[Random Soldier]
Sir. Thank you, sir.
[Captain Timoth]
This is for a Mimir, you say? That's as good a way as any to spread this news. We're looking to take Ribcage, and there ain't a thing they can do about it. Let them shiver when they hear this and let them know that the attack will come within a year's time. Probably through the Great Pass. You know, I like the look of you. Let me see that plaque (sounds of breaking). Well, well, well. Look at that. Walking around Rigus without a ranking. Looks like you're at my mercy now. Troopers!
[Random Soldier]
Sir! Yes, sir!
[Captain Timoth]
Escort our new recruit to the induction center!
[Random Soldiee]
Sir! Yes, sir!

[[File:A Player's Primer to the Outlands CD.jpg|300px|right]] ''The Caverns of Thought'' is the 26th track on the audio CD portion of '''[[A Player's Primer to the Outlands]]'''. == Transcript == : '''Mimir''': [[Illithid]]s — or mind flayers, as they are more commonly known — place their power in a winding maze of tunnels near the [[Dwarven Mountain]]. It's actually connected to both the Mountain and [[Gzemnid's Realm]]. But a traveler who passes into [[Ilsensine]]'s [[Caverns of Thought]] will know it: the mental drone becomes steadily worse as a body penetrates farther into the realm. [[Isusslis]], an illithid traveler, speaks of the Caverns of Thought: : '''Isusslis''': From the Cavern of Thought, stay away! Friendly advice, give I. Though brains eat people my, given heed this advice. What? Speak I you for? Do not go to the caverns. Ilsensine will your brains suck dry, taking thoughts for itself. The brain-god hate non-illithid destroy. Even fiends steer clear of caverns. Their brains eat good as anyone. Mark my words: caverns dangerous. Do not go in. == Background Information == * The voice actors for both Isusslis and the Mimir repeatedly use "Ilsenine" erroneously, when the illithid god's name is "Ilsensine," with two S's. We used the correct name in the transcript above. * Although Isusslis' speech initially seems Yoda-esque, fitting a repeatable pattern, it quickly devolves, with words within a sentence mixed in random order, before returning to something approaching normal at "Speak I for you," suggesting they're intentionally making their speech more understandable for the listener's benefit. They may be a [[Xaositect]], naturally speaking in Chaosspeak. ** The beginning dialogue should be translated: "Stay away from the Caverns of Thought! I give friendly advice. Though my people eat brains, heed this advice given. What? I speak for you?" == External Links == [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pTbeJSkLCBw This track on YouTube] {| class="fandom-table browser" style="width:100%" | class="prev"|'''Previous Track'''

[[File:A Player's Primer to the Outlands CD.jpg|300px|right]] ''The Great Pass'' is the 32nd track on the audio CD portion of '''[[A Player's Primer to the Outlands]]'''. == Transcript == : '''Mimir''': Cutting through the [[Vale of the Spine]], and connecting [[Ribcage]] to [[Rigus]], lies the [[Great Pass]]. The Pass is said to be controlled by a small bandit army. It's for this reason that many merchants making the Ribcage-Rigus circuit take the long way. One such merchant is [[Terennius Red]]: : '''Terennius Red''': The bandits ain't the only reason I don't go through the Pass anymore. I can take a small hit in my profits. I didn't complain about [[Quentill Paracs|Paracs]] or General [[Nagaro|what's-her-name]] from Rigus, but both sorts threatened to have me executed, or worse, for spreading fear among the merchants. So, I let it drop. Anyways, the main reason I don't go there no more is that I've seen armies start to cordon off both ends of the Pass like they're getting ready for war on both sides. While I'd like to think that Paracs and the General listened to me, I think there's something much more dangerous going on. And I ain't gonna get my [indecipherable] muddied. == Background Information == * The Great Pass is a track that doesn't have an accompanying section in the Primer book. The Pass material is instead included in the section on [[Ribcage]]. == External Links == [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tcUCqxawfTs This track on YouTube] {| class="fandom-table browser" style="width:100%" | class="prev"|'''Previous Track'''

[[File:A Player's Primer to the Outlands CD.jpg|300px|right]] ''The Great Road'' is the 39th track on the audio CD portion of '''[[A Player's Primer to the Outlands]]'''. == Transcript == : '''Mimir''': The [[Outer Planes]] can be imagined as a Great Ring, with the [[Outlands]] in the center, and the city of [[Sigil]] in the center of the Outlands. There is said to be a road linking all the planes to each other, one that can be traveled by a being with determination. [[Dae Zeka]] tells us more: : '''Dae Zeka''': The path that links all the planes is called the [[Great Road]]! Since the planes are all in a ring around the Outlands, it's not hard to imagine. Sometimes the Road's paved, more often, it's not. There's permanent gates that don't need keys abutting the neighboring planes, and towns spring up around these, so if you wanted to walk all the way from [[Elysium]] and back without passing through the same place, you could. You'd need the permission of the fiends in the [[Lower Planes]] to walk on their portion of the Great Road. And I don't know of anyone or anything that's walked the whole Ring except the [[Great Modron March|Modron Procession]]. It's a good way to get lost. Besides, folks get mighty leery of people just "passing through." If you're thinking about doing the walk, do it carefully. == Background Information == * ''The Great Road'' is the final informational track on the CD. == External Links == [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=glWNbFNkpUI This track on YouTube] {| class="fandom-table browser" style="width:100%" | class="prev"|'''Previous Track'''

[[File:A Player's Primer to the Outlands CD.jpg|300px|right]] ''The Hinterlands'' is the 34th track on the audio CD portion of '''[[A Player's Primer to the Outlands]]'''. == Transcript == : '''Mimir''': Vast stretches on the infinite [[Outlands|plane]] are unexplored and unknown. Their secrets remain dark to the eyes of mortals. Listen to [[David Zerins]]: : '''David Zerins''': Hey! You've gotta help me, I've been out here for days on end trying to get back to Sigil! Which way's spireward? Which way, eh?! C'mon! : Sorry 'bout that. I've just been real worried that the first sod I've run across was going to be a fiend or something worse. And so naturally the sight of you fills me with relief. I'm babbling again, aren't I? I've been across all the Outlands, it seems, from the tallest mountain to the lowest valley, from rivers that make Prime worlds look small to the barest trickle of a spring in the desert. And not once in all that time did I run across a road. : There're cities out there. Whole civilizations, I tell you. But I was too scared to check 'em out! I don't think they was even humanoid, you know? There's more of them than anyone knows, and it's a lot different than they might think. I tried to go back to one of the cities, and came across a ruin that was nothing like the city I saw there before. Even the landscape around was completely different! : Time messes with you out here. And there's no telling how it's going to be. : So. Let's get back to the [[Spire]]. Why are you shaking your head? Are you lost too?! == Background Information == * The "time messes with you out here" line has a faint echo on the words, but played in reverse, such that the echo precedes the words. == External Links == [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SELJxY4MFwM This track on YouTube] {| class="fandom-table browser" style="width:100%" | class="prev"|'''Previous Track'''

revision.text:
[[File:A Player's Primer to the Outlands CD.jpg|300px|right]] ''The Modron Procession'' is the 37th track on the audio CD portion of '''[[A Player's Primer to the Outlands]]'''. == Transcript == : '''Mimir''': This is [[Keeleg Boulier]], speaking of the Modron Procession: : '''Keeleg Boulier''': Periodically, though the exact period is not known, a great [[modron]] army marches out from the inner reaches of [[Mechanus]], and makes its way across the [[Great Ring]], sometimes heading through [[Arcadia]], sometimes through [[Acheron]]. These armies are comprised of varying shapes and sizes, with nary a group the same. : Few of the modron hierarchs accompany the Great March, instead, attending to their duties in Mechanus. However, there are great masses of the lesser modrons, each of which is under the command of one greater. The purpose of these walkabouts is dark. Some sages speculate that the modrons are gathering information about the state of the multiverse, so that the modrons can calibrate the gears of Mechanus accordingly. Others say that the Great March is simply a modron plot to usurp the universe, that they're gathering information for their armies. : Since modron energy is never lost, the creatures as a whole suffer no real damage during the March, and can always return to report on their findings. Whatever the true purpose of the Procession, it's something that scares the fiend out of people simply because they don't know what it's for. : '''Army General''': Retreat! Retreat! == Background Information == * Although a number of different terms were used early in Planescape, later products settled on the "[[Great Modron March]]" as the official title of the Procession. * Likewise the exact period between Marches (17 cycles of the largest gear of Mechanus, each cycle lasting 17 years = 172 = 289 years) wasn't solidified initially. == External Links == [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=k2zpjSeiC74 This track on YouTube] {| class="fandom-table browser" style="width:100%" | class="prev"|'''Previous Track'''

revision.text:
['''Mimir''']
Every petitioner who answers to the celestial bureaucracy, also known as the Chinese pantheon, must come to the Palace of Judgment for assignment in the afterlife.
[Random Female 1]
You'd think somebody who died as horribly as I did a little special consideration.
[Random Male 1]
How much longer is this going to take?
[Random Male 2]
I'm sorry, form 179 B, not 179 C. That means another 16-month wait.
[Random Male 3]
This time I want to come back as a mage.
[Random Male 4]
It wasn't as if this was the first time it ever happened.
['''Mimir''']
It has the second greatest concentration of gates in the multiverse, second only to the City of Doors itself. A body hoping to use these gates must first receive permission from the bureaucracy. A process that could literally take years. Chen Yu, a go Zu factotum, or guide, tells of the palace of judgment.
[Chen Yu]
I have seen it all, honored, master. There are millions who come through here every year, and each of them has their own story to tell.
[Random Female 2]
It wasn't as if I meant to take that ???.
[Random Female 3]
There I was without a stitch on.
[Random Male 5]
The king swore he would pardon me.
[Random Male 6]
Uh, exactly how many murders does it take before you're considered a mass murderer?
[Random Female 4]
All right, so I took one tainty little dragon egg.
[Chen Yu]
Some of them are honest, some blatant liars. Nearly all of them are frightened senseless by the knowledge that they will receive their just deserts here in the palace. Of course, nothing is done without the accompanying permits from the Celestial Bureaucracy.
Oh dear. Form 9.17 has been misfiled. You'll have to do that one over and all the supporting documents. Now, if you will, sir. You are not permitted in there. No, wait. That's a gate to Acheron. Fool!

[[File:A Player's Primer to the Outlands CD.jpg|300px|right]] ''The Vale of the Spine'' is the 31st track on the audio CD portion of '''[[A Player's Primer to the Outlands]]'''. == Transcript == : '''Mimir''': Everyone knows that the town of [[Ribcage]] is nestled in the [[Vale of the Spine]] like a malignant heart. ['''Mimir'''] The gate town for Gehenna is Torch. It's built on the side of volcanic mountain above of all that's pestilential. The chant is, that Torch never stops, that there's always a deal going on and a tavern always open. The most famous tavern is the Festival of the falling Coins operated by a drow named Gutter.
[drow named Cutter.]
What can I do for you, cutter? You want an information about Torch, do you? You've come to the right blood. I know just about everything that goes on in this pitiful excuse for a town, and I can tell you for a price. That's a good piece of jink you got there, my friend. Now, you want I should tell you about the six thieves' guilds or that you'd best be perry in this town. There are those here who wouldn't even try to peel you. They just stick a shiv in your ribs and leave you. I can tell you about the gate hovering hundreds of feet above the ground. and the best way to get to it. I could even tell you that a people of Torch among the worst in all the Outlands. Greedy for money and power, willing to do whatever it takes to get either one. Take for example, the basher behind you. I think he's looking for your purse. Oh dear. I guess he's looking for your life, too, hehehe!

['''Mimir''']
Walking Castles, as described by Limoney Gabledrop, called "The Mad" by some.
[Liony Gable Drop]
Hey, you want to know about walking castles, hey, berk? I can tell you all about the one I ran into. I was traveling with my fiance Clarissa and a party of our friends back from Funnel and we were walking to a portal we knew of in the second ring.
[Male]
It's raining!
[Clarissa]
Find shelter!
[Male]
Over there, look!
(to many talking at once, couldn’t make out)
[Clarissa]
Come on.
[Male?]
It wet.
The nearest shelter was a decrepit looking hut like an ancient Hermitage. But that didn't look like it was being used. I mean like a bunch of clueless sods, we figured that it meant it wasn't and we bolted in doors. (good, huh?), it turned out to be a lot bigger on the inside than we expected, and a lot better decorated, but none of us took that to mean that anything was a miss. Clarissa picked up some jade figurine that was sitting on a shelf littered with jade figurines and promptly dropped it. (Oops). Suddenly the whole hut shakes, like it's been hit by an earthquake
[Male]
Quick! the door!
We ran to the door, and see the ground dropping away like we'd been lost into space, shooting us thousands of feet into the air! Below the hut an enormous pair of goat legs pushed the Hut from the ground, leaving a crater the size of a small moon and the legs started running. And fast! It turned out that the hut's just an observation room on the top of a mobile tower, and apparently, the owner decided to pick up and leave! Well, discretion being the better part of valour, I hide behind a potted plant. Just in time too. Some horrid abomination that bitter belongs in the slimes spawning pits of the Abyss burst through the floor and engulfs Clarissa!
[screams of Clarissa]
[Limoney Gabledrop]
Then it looks around and sees our friends. The lucky ones jumped out the door and died easy. The screaming of the others will echo in my head until the furies come to take me. I don't know how I was overlooked, but I'll tell you one thing, berk: when the castle settled down again, I ran so fast and so far that my feet didn't touch the ground until the first ring. And I'll never, never, never, get closer than miles away from another Walking Castle.

page.title: Abellio

revision.text:
'''Abellio''' was the first layer of [[Arcadia]] in the [[Great Wheel cosmology]]. An endless stretch of orderly plains dotted with a few mountains and hills, it contained the [[divine realm]]s of [[Clangeddin Silverbeard]] and [[Marduk]].<ref name="PL2e-p12-17">{{Cite book/Planes of Law/Arcadia|12-17}}</ref><ref name="MP3e-p130-132">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|130-132}}</ref><ref name="OHG2e-172">{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|172}}</ref>
==Geography== The large flat expanse of Abellio was a land of plenty. There were abundant forests, lakes, rivers, and open fields. In the harmonious ecosystem, even wild beasts contributed to the common good.<ref name="PL2e-p12-17" /><ref name="MP3e-p130-132" />
Abellio was a well-ordered place with well-tended crops, orchards, and cities all laid out in regular geometric shapes. Properly shaped and arranged flowerbeds of every color were always in bloom and never needed a gardener, nourished by gentle rains. Night and day were provided by a huge rotating sphere, half radiant, half dark, set into the highest mountain in the plane. The trees of Abellio grew in straight orchard rows or tidy forests. They had bark of [[iron]], [[copper]], [[silver]], or [[gold]], depending on the type of tree. The leaves resembled those of [[Prime Material Plane]] trees but were colored dark green to fire red and never fell to the ground. Each type of tree constantly produced a particular fruit which had magical properties like a [[potion]] when consumed.<ref name="MotP1e-86">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|86}}</ref>
==Trade== The main trade post of Abellio was the district of [[Mercantus]], the portion of the city of [[Mandible (city)|Mandible]] that was above ground. It welcomed traders and travelers to its markets and inns.<ref name="PL2e-p12-17" /><ref name="MP3e-p130-132" />
==Notable Locations== * [[Mandible (city)|Mandible]], a highly militaristic hive-city inhabited by [[formian]]s, and the layer's main trading post. It was ruled by the Queen Mother [[K'l'tk'thra]].<ref name="PL2e-p12-17" /><ref name="MP3e-p130-132" />
* [[Marduk (realm)|Marduk]], the divine realm of the [[Untheric pantheon|Untheric]] deity Marduk. A dry and arid land, it still allowed trees to grow and streams to flow. It was inhabited by a peaceful and mostly complacent population.<ref name="PL2e-p12-17" />
* [[Mount Clangeddin]], the divine realm of Clangeddin Silverbeard. It was a perfectly conical mountain that rose about {{SI|30000|ft|long=yes}} at its cloudy and stormy peak, whose interior had been expertly and luxuriously carved and decorated. Visitors were welcome in its halls, in particular for the purpose of ordering weapons from the expert smiths that worked on the mountain's forges.<ref name="PL2e-p12-17" /><ref name="MP3e-p130-132" />

If there's anything you don't like, you'll find it here. |A [[tanar'ri]] saying.{{Cite book/Planes of Chaos/The Book of Chaos|12}} }} ==Cosmology== In the [[Great Wheel cosmology]] model, the Abyss was an [[Outer plane]] on the Great Wheel connected to the [[Astral plane]], [[Pandemonium]], [[Carceri]], and the [[Outlands]].{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|74}} Some estimated that the Abyss had 666 layers,{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|99}} while the [[Fraternity of Order]] claimed to have catalogued 679 layers.{{Cite book/Planes of Chaos/The Book of Chaos|20}} It was possible that the number of layers was infinite, but no one could be certain. The first layer, named Pazunia after the demon lord [[Pazuzu]], was described as a barren, dusty place baking under a red sun, broken only by great [[iron]] fortresses, huge holes in the ground, and the river [[Styx]]. Some branches of the Styx flowed down the holes (which were conduits to the various layers) and some of these holes supplied water to the Styx in reverse waterfalls. When the Great Wheel model was replaced by the [[World Tree cosmology]] model, the river Styx was renamed the [[River of Blood]] and it flowed through all the [[fiendish planes]] (except for the [[Supreme Throne]] and the [[Demonweb Pits]]) originating in the Abyss, passing through the [[Blood Rift]]—an unusual plane that connected the Abyss with the [[Nine Hells]]{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|140}}—bringing the demons even closer to their arch-enemies the [[devil]]s,{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|141}} resulting in the [[Blood War]]. Cosmologists found evidence of portals between the Abyss and the [[Barrens of Doom and Despair]], [[Clangor]], the [[Demonweb Pits]], and [[Hammergrim]], with intermittent portals to [[Deep Caverns]] and [[Fated Depths]]. The [[Astral plane]] connected all of the fiendish planes to the [[Prime Material Plane]], but not directly to each other.{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|139}} [[File:The Abyss.jpg|thumb|300px|''[[Asmodeus]] and his armies attacking demons in the [[Blood War]].'']] After the [[Spellplague]], [[Asmodeus]] consumed the essence of the fallen [[Azuth]] and ended the Blood War by casting the Abyss to the furthest depths of the [[Elemental Chaos]].{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|73}} The [[World Axis cosmology]] described the ruined Abyss as a domain with ever-changing features and realms, where the demons waged futile wars over meaningless empires. Once again the river Styx flowed through the [[Nine Hells]] and the Abyss, but then emptied its pollution into the [[Astral Sea]].{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|64,66}} Other than the Styx or braving the Elemental Chaos, the only known passages to the Abyss were found in the [[Demonweb Pits]], the [[Dismal Caverns]], and [[Nishrek]]. ==Layers== [[Image:Abyss Map.jpg|300px|thumb|right|An artist's rendering of the Abyss]] {{main|Layers of the Abyss}} The number of layers in the Abyss was unknown and perhaps unknowable, with at least 679 having been catalogued{{Cite book/Planes of Chaos/The Book of Chaos|19-20}} but this article attempts to list them regardless of which cosmology model was in favor at the time of discovery. Each layer had its own characteristics, which were as varied as the demons themselves. All types of terrain, atmosphere, weather, gravity, and material composition were represented in the myriad layers. Some examples were: * [[Planar traits#Elemental and Energy Traits|Air-dominant]]—zero gravity, no matter except air * Ash—blowing dunes of ashes * Battleground—[[Blood War]] or other * City—warrens and slums to citadels and palaces, teeming with demons * [[Planar traits#Elemental and Energy Traits|Earth-dominant]]—solid rock tunneled by the inhabitants * [[Planar traits#Elemental and Energy Traits|Fire-dominant]]—everburning flames with [[salamander]]s, ''etc''. * Delusion—appears to be Normal but the flowers are poisonous or the trees attack * Desert—endless tracts of black, white, or red sand with no water * Glacier—infinite black, white, or orange ice with few rocky peaks breaking the surface * Hellscape—a burning mix of magma, rock, and belching brimstone * Maelstrom—swirling, bubbling chaos like [[Limbo]] * Mountainous—rocky crags, precipitous cliffs, soaring peaks * [[Planar traits#Elemental and Energy Traits|Negative-dominant]]—major or minor * Normal—similar to a Prime plane with various flora and fauna * Ocean—a trackless ocean, with a surface * Salt—crystalline badlands or desert * Sea—of acid, blood, garbage, insects, oil, or worms, ''etc''. * Swamp—noisome bog inhabited by predators * Undead—[[specter]]s, spooks, and [[ghost]]s * Volcanic—lava flows, earthquakes, volcanoes, and smoke * [[Planar traits#Elemental and Energy Traits|Water-dominant]]—nightmarish creatures in the murk Despite its name and notoriety for being never-ending, it was not known whether the layers of the Abyss were truly infinite in number.The Abyss is often listed as infinite but so are the other Outer Planes, or, as per ''[[Manual of the Planes 3rd edition]]'', "at least so large that they may as well be infinite." Part of the reason for this was that some places might have been so absolutely inhospitable that none, not mortal, nor god, nor demon lords themselves could survive (the deeper layers reportedly having been even worse in the past), and hence were not known about.{{Cite dragon/349/Demonomicon of Iggwilv: Dagon: Prince of Darkened Depths|31}}{{Cite book/Demonomicon|8, 42-43}} While the hundreds of layers of the Abyss might seem to utterly eclipse all other Outer planes put together, this figure was misleading. Besides the issue of uninhabitability, layers and [[divine realm]]s, the personal territories of [[power]]s, were often one in the same in the Abyss, whereas other planes often had several realms on one layer. Exacerbating the problem, and another reason why the Abyssal layers could not be properly counted, was that the number was always in a state of flux.{{Cite book/Faces of Evil: The Fiends|62-63}} [[File:Alkilith-5e.png|thumb|right|250px|An alkilith weakens the fabric of reality, opening a window into the Abyss.]] In the very depths of the Abyss, the heart of the plane was constantly cleaving through the primal foundations of the cosmos, as it had since before the dawn of mortals, spawning new layers. Arguably worse, if a demonic invasion was allowed to fester, entire worlds could fall into the Abyss, becoming the basis of new layers and realms.{{Cite book/Mordenkainen's Tome of Foes|25-26}} Conversely, the Abyss was also capable of losing layers. The individual layers of the Abyss had primal urges and a constant need for nourishment, shrinking and weakened until nothing was left if not fed. Alternatively, they might be absorbed by other layers, only able to escape this state by acquiring sufficient sustenance. Occassionally the battling of demons over control of a layer could become so cataclysmic that the entire realm was outright obliterated. Layers could also be intentionally removed, such as when [[Lolth]] expended much of her divine energy seperating the [[Demonweb Pits]],{{Cite book/Annihilation/Paperback|311}} or when a pantheon of offended deities ripped out and condensed a demon lord's entire layer (with him still in it) and cast it into the [[Astral plane]]. Despite this ending in the Abyss, much like a hungry, rudely awakened beast, almost instantly striking down the entire pantheon in that case, the attack itself was successful, leaving nothing but a void and their own decomposing divine corpses.{{Cite dragon/357/Demonomicon of Iggwilv: Demogorgon: Prince of Demons|30}} {{Fq | width = 300px | source = [[Mordenkainen]] | text = Some scholars number and name the parts of the Abyss, declaring that this demon lord or that rules a portion of the place. When your house is on fire, does it matter what the flames look like in each room? Should you bother to give them names? What's important is escaping and putting out any fire that clings to you. }} It was also a possibility that destroyed layers were capable of being reborn elsewhere in the Abyss, although this was not a certainty. This was ignoring the fact that layers were shaped by the conscious manipulations and subconscious wills of its resident demon lord, and so even the nature of a single layer could become obsolete by the time such information was established. ==Inhabitants== {{main|Demon}} There were myriad types of [[demon]]s, too numerous to catalog here, but including the [[tanar'ri]], [[obyrith]]s, and [[loumara]]s. Non-demonic life could be found in the Abyss as well, with both mortal explorers and captives and the [[petitioner]]s brought there after death. Many wicked [[deities]] also based themselves here.{{Cite book/Fiendish Codex I: Hordes of the Abyss|107-109}} ==Afterlife== {{Main|Afterlife}} Beliefs about the journey of souls to the afterlife changed with the shifting [[cosmology|cosmologies]] and the [[crystal sphere]] in which one resided. In some worlds, [[chaotic evil]] souls would travel directly to the Abyss and become [[mane]]s, the lowest form of sub-demon.{{Cite book/Monster Manual 1st edition|17}} Manes were treated as slaves, cannon fodder, and food by the demon lords.{{Cite book/Demonomicon|26}} For mortals of [[Realmspace]], however, all souls would first go to the [[Fugue Plane]] and await transport to their final resting place.{{Cite book/Faiths and Avatars|2-3}}{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|153}} Greedy demon lords would open a portal to the Fugue Plane and conduct raids to steal souls and bring them back to the Abyss to become manes.{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition|259}} After the [[Spellplague]], [[Shar]] reshaped the [[Plane of Shadow]] and folded in what death energy did not get absorbed into the [[Elemental Chaos]] and created the [[Shadowfell]].{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|69}} After that, souls on their way to the afterlife started their journey in the Shadowfell and most made it to the Fugue Plane to await judgment, but a few remained behind or were lost.{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|65}} ==Powers== Relatively few [[Greater deity|greater powers]] carved out a realm in the Abyss because dealing with the ubiquitous hordes of demons and ambitious [[demon lord]]s would require too much of their attention. Those deities for whom the chaotic evil nature of the Abyss was attractive at some point in time, along with the demon "royalty" whose names were not spoken openly in civil society, were: * [[Ahazu]] the Seizer.{{Cite book/Monster Manual II 1st edition|35}} * [[Baphomet]]{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|143}} created an [[Endless Maze]] that changed form as it passed between layers. It was populated by a variety of [[minotaur]]s said to have breath weapons or magical abilities.{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|176}} * [[Beshaba]], the Goddess of Mischief and Maid of Misfortune once made her home in the Abyss.{{Cite book/Cyclopedia of the Realms|10}}{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Adventures|16}} * [[Dagon]] controlled a watery layer filled with [[hezrou]] and aquatic [[dretch]]. * [[Demogorgon]] controlled several layers, each filled with dinosaurs, wild apes, and flying monsters as well as the usual demonkind. * [[Diinkarazan]], crazed twin brother of [[derro]] deity [[Diirinka]], was held by a curse in the [[Prison of the Mad God]], the [[Layers of the Abyss#Layer 586: Prison of the Mad God|586{{th}} layer]].{{Cite book/Monster Mythology|65}}{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|83}} * [[Eltab]] lurked on this plane in the "[[Hidden Layer]]". * [[Fraz-Urb'luu]] had a realm that reportedly rivaled the beauty of the [[Twin Paradises]] or [[Arvandor]] but it was an illusion covering decay and rotting flesh. * [[Garyx]] the All-Destroyer, [[Draconic pantheon|dragon god]] of [[fire]], made his lair somewhere in the Abyss.{{Cite book/Cult of the Dragon|120}}{{Cite book/Draconomicon (1990)|25-26}}The more recent but Core source ''[[Races of the Dragon]]'' places Garyx in [[Pandemonium]] instead, which more closely fits his alignment between chaotic evil and chaotic neutral. * [[Gorellik]], the abandoned god of the [[gnoll]]s, spent much of his time wandering the Abyss.{{Cite book/Planes of Chaos/The Book of Chaos|9}} * [[Grankhul]], the hunter god of the [[bugbear]]s,{{Cite book/Demihuman Deities|151}} had the 241st layer, [[Palpitatia]], as divine realm.{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|175}} * [[Graz'zt]] had a great palace that other. * [[Kali]], the feared Black Earth Mother of the [[Vedic pantheon]], held sway over both the [[Layers of the Abyss#Layer 500: Unnamed|500th layer]], and the [[Caverns of the Skull]], the [[Layers of the Abyss#Layer 643: Caverns of the Skull|663rd layer]].{{Cite book/Fiendish Codex I: Hordes of the Abyss|156-157}}{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|155}} * [[Kostchtchie]] controlled only part of a layer, but his ice palace was filled with creatures of cold. * [[Laogzed]], god of [[troglodyte]]s, had a realm called the [[Rotting Plain]] here.{{Cite book/Deities & Demigods 1st edition|112}}{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|177}} * [[Lolth]]{{Cite book/Deities & Demigods 1st edition|107}} spun her webs on the 65th layer in the midst of a maelstrom that was the portal to her abode on the 66th layer{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|102,103}} before she became a [[greater deity|greater god]] and removed her [[Demonweb Pits]] from the Abyss to join the [[fiendish plane]]s.{{Cite book/Player’s Guide to Faerûn|149}} After the [[Spellplague]] her realm survived to float in the [[Astral Sea]].{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|63,74}} * [[Merrshaulk]], the ancient [[yuan-ti]] deity, resided on the 74{{th}} layer called [[Smaragd]]. * [[Moander]], the Rotting God, had a realm called [[Offalmound]] on the 223rd layer, also known as Rarandreth, before his demise.{{Cite book/Faiths & Avatars|119}}{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|182}} * [[Obox-ob]] once had a realm here called [[Zionyn]]. * [[Orcus]] had an enormous palace made of bones, rising out of a field of bone dust. He employed many [[undead]] as his guards and servants. * [[The Pack (fiends)|The Pack]], a group of powerful entities worshiped by the [[leucrotta]], roamed the Abyss in search of prey (usually tanar'ri).{{Cite book/Elminster's Ecologies/The Great Gray Land of Thar|14-15}} * [[Pale Night]], the Mother of Demons, lived in a bone castle in the maze of Baphomet{{Cite book/Fiendish Codex I: Hordes of the Abyss|152-154}} and controlled her own layer called ''Androlynne''. * [[Pazuzu]] had no real home but controlled the skies above every layer of the Abyss. He, like [[Charon]] on the [[Styx]], controlled a primary mode of travel in the Abyss and was respected if not feared. * The [[Queen of Chaos]] ruled the fourteenth layer called the ''Steaming Fen''. * [[Ramenos]], the deity of the [[bullywug]]s, slumbered on the 74{{th}} layer most of the time, sharing Merrshaulk's realm of Smaragd.{{Cite book/Monster Mythology|78}} * [[Skiggaret]], the bugbear [[Ocanthus]] | layer-number-GW = | location-GW = | refs-GW = {{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|73}}{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|78-82}} | type-WA = | shape-size-WA = | gravity-WA = | mutability-WA = | element-energy-WA = | alignment-WA = | magical-WA = | layers-WA = | layer-number-WA = | location-WA = | refs-WA = | type-WT = | shape-size-WT = | gravity-WT = | time-WT = | morphic-WT = | element-energy-WT = | alignment-WT = | magical-WT = | faith-WT = | layers-WT = | layer-number-WT = | location-WT = | refs-WT = | inhabitants = yes | deities = yes | locations = yes | organizations = yes | settlements = yes | based = [[wikipedia:en:Acheron|Acheron]] (Greek) | usethe = | useon = }}The '''Infinite Battlefield of Acheron'''{{Cite book/Dungeon Master's Guide 5th edition|58}} ({{Pronounce|ÆTCH|ur|un|refs={{Cite dragon/93/Ay pronunseeAYshun gyd|25}}|audio=Acheron.ogg}}) was an [[Outer Plane]] in the [[Great Wheel cosmology]] model representing alignments between [[lawful evil]] and [[lawful neutral]] with emphasis on law. Some characteristics of this plane were ascribed to the [[World Tree cosmology]] planes of [[Clangor]],{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|147}} [[Nishrek]],{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|161}} and [[Warrior's Rest]]{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|163}} when that cosmology became popular. Nishrek and Warrior's Rest survived the [[Spellplague]] and became part of the [[World Axis cosmology]] model.{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|64,65}} {{Quote |Acheron is the home of dreams gone wrong. |[[Deva]] Isab of the Bent Wing.{{Cite book/Planes of Law/Acheron|2}} }} ==Description== Acheron was the bridge between the ultimate order of [[Nirvana]] and the regimented evil of the [[Nine Hells]] and as such, each layer emphasized order over evil. The land masses on each layer were blocks of geometric simplicity the size of nations floating in a sea of air. The blocks would slowly collide and part without causing any upheaval or tremor, allowing beings to move to a new block if desired. The dance of the blocks was carefully orchestrated and creatures of high intelligence could usually discern a pattern for an area by studying the motions. It was said gravity pulled toward the center of the blocks but in practical terms gravity was normal to each surface. ===Avalas=== {{Main|Avalas}} Acheron was sometimes known as the "iron-shod battle planes of Acheron" due to the characteristics of the first layer, Avalas. The blocks of the top plane were black with a metallic hardness that allowed the sounds of battle and troop movements to reverberate loudly. Avalas had the most block-like worlds and the highest population as the armies of the [[Outer Planes]] spent their [[afterlife]] clashing in neutral territory over differences both subtle and gross. The landscape consisted of cone-shaped mountains and pits plus the iron fortresses of the various armies. The only other remarkable feature of this layer was the river [[Styx]] that would bubble up from one pit, meander across two or three sides of a block, and then disappear down another pit. The Styx did not visit all the blocks, but those it did could be reached by [[Charon]] and his servants. Avalas touched the [[Astral Plane]] and had spherical portals to the three adjacent planes: [[Nirvana]], the [[Nine Hells]], and [[Concordant Opposition]]. The portals hung at fixed locations in space and would pass harmlessly through the blocks, becoming inactive while inside a block and reactivating when they reappeared. Anyone emerging from a portal would start to fall toward the nearest block and almost certainly required some form of flight to avoid a high velocity impact. The portals were activated by touch and the destination could be determined by the sound it made when activated. A harmonious chord indicated a portal to Nirvana, a dissonant chord meant the Nine Hells, and silence indicated Concordant Opposition. Avalas was the location of the [[orc]] realm of [[Nishrek]]{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|177}} and the [[goblin]] realm of [[Clangor]].{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|176}} [[Bane]]'s realm, ''the Black Bastion'', was also on Avalas.{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|182}} [[Gilgeam]]'s realm [[Zigguraxus]] existed here until that god's death.{{Cite book/Powers & Pantheons|102}} ===Thuldanin=== {{/Imagemap}} {{Main|Thuldanin}} This layer was the [[wikipedia:en:Sargasso Sea|Sargasso Sea]], [[wikipedia:en:Elephants' graveyard|Elephants' graveyard]], and scrap heap for countless contraptions, creations, weapons, armor, failed experiments, broken devices, fallen buildings, and shipwrecks of sea and air. The blocks of Thuldanin were hollow and pockmarked with pits that lead to the interior a few miles/kilometers down. There the flotsam and jetsam of the ages turned to stone in a matter of days or weeks due to the magic of this layer. Thuldanin had no inhabitants, only the occasional visitor from Avalas looking for some piece of magic or technology that might turn the tide of battle. [[Laduguer]]'s realm ''Hammergrim'' was here.{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|172}} ===Tintibulus=== {{Main|Tintibulus}} The third layer of Acheron had blocks different than those of the other layers. Here the blocks were made of gray volcanic stone and the faces were six-sided, eight-sided, or even higher in number of edges. When the blocks of Tintibulus collided the surfaces would fracture along natural fault lines into hexagons great and small. This layer had no inhabitants but was attractive to magical researchers for its emptiness and isolation. ===Ocanthus=== {{Main|Ocanthus}} The blocks of the fourth and final layer were square and so razor-thin as to be almost two-dimensional. They ranged in size from a few inches/centimeters to several miles/kilometers across. Both sides of the hard black squares had normal gravity pulling to the surface and could be walked upon. Being hit by the edge of one of these razor-sharp squares could be deadly. ==Inhabitants== The main inhabitants of Acheron were the spirit legions occupying Avalas. They were made up of the spirits of [[human]]s, [[dwarves]], [[halfling]]s, [[ogre]]s, and many other mindless soldiers who died in wars after forgetting their purpose; those for whom war became an end in itself. The spirits would congregate with others of similar beliefs or alignment and form nations on the surface of a block. They would fight to control a block and then join forces to conquer another block when it came within their reach. Legion members who were slain in battle would return with full strength within 24 hours, ready to fight again. The [[orc]] and [[goblinoid]] spirit legions shared the same large block in Avalas and besieged one another regularly.{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 1st edition|114}} Other creatures that could be found in Acheron were wandering [[imp]]s, [[rust monster]]s, [[achaierai]], and occasionally [[devil]]s and [[modron]]s. ==Realms== * [[Bahgtru]], son of Gruumsh, held a realm on a smaller block which orbited Gruumsh's block. * [[Bane]], God of Strife, Hatred, and Tyranny, once had a realm in Acheron{{Cite book/Cyclopedia of the Realms|10}}{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Adventures|37}} before he was slain by [[Torm]] during the [[Time of Troubles]].{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Setting 3rd edition|238}} After his resurrection, he carved out a realm in the [[Barrens of Doom and Despair]] as described by the [[World Tree cosmology]] model.{{Cite book/Player's Guide to Faerûn|145}} (After the [[Spellplague]] he had his own realm, [[Banehold]], that floated in the [[Astral Sea]] as described by the [[World Axis cosmology]] model.{{Cite book/Forgotten Realms Campaign Guide|62}}) * [[Deep Duerra]] maintained the [[Citadel of Thought]] in Thuldanin.{{Cite book/Demihuman Deities|62}} * [[Gilgeam]], Supreme Ruler of [[Unther]], had his realm, [[Zigguraxus]], on Avalas. * [[Gruumsh]] of the [[orc]]s at one time made his home, [[Nishrek]], consisting of several large citadels, on a large block in the first layer.{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|133}} * [[Ilneval]], lieutenant of Gruumsh, had holdings on a smaller block which orbited Gruumsh's block. * [[Khurgorbaeyag]], [[goblin]] god of slavery and patron of the [[Batiri]], resided in his pantheon's realm of [[Clangor]] in [[Avalas]].{{Cite book/Demihuman Deities|85}}{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|132}} * [[Laduguer]], the Gray Protector of the [[duergar]], maintained his realm of [[Hammergrim]] on Thuldanin.{{Cite book/Demihuman Deities|71}} * [[Luthic]], the cave goddess and wife of Gruumsh, lived on a smaller block that orbited Gruumsh's block. * [[Maglubiyet]], war god of the [[goblin]]s and [[hobgoblin]]s, shared the same block as Gruumsh and maintained citadels as well in the never-ending battle between these hated enemies. His realm was named Clangor. * [[Nomog-Geaya]], the divine General of the hobgoblins, resided with his superior in Clangor. ==Appendix== ===Appearances=== :;Novels ::{{Refonly}} ::''[[Shadowdale (novel)|Shadowdale]]'' ===References=== {{Refs}} ===Connections=== {{Acheron}} {{Cosmologies}} [[Category:Outer Planes]] [[Category:Great Wheel planes]] [[Category:Planes of law]] [[Category:Planes of existence]] [[Category:Locations in the Outer Planes]] [[Category:Locations in the Great Wheel planes]] [[Category:Locations]] [[Category:Lower Planes]] [[Category:Locations on the River Styx]]

'''Aebrynis''' is the primary inhabited world found within [[w:c:spelljammer:Aebrynisspace|an unknown crystal sphere]] on the [[Prime Material plane]].
Many planars consider it "hardly worth noting," with few portals or sites of interest to planewalkers. It does, however, have some connections to a plane called the Shadow World. Once a realm of spirit and faerie called the Spirit World, it has gradually succumbed to the leftover taint from the destroyed Azrai. It's as though the local [[Feywild]] was gradually transforming into the [[Shadowfell]].<ref name="pwhb31">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|page=31}}</ref><ref name="pwhb147">{{b|Planescape|The Planewalker's Handbook|pdf=17280|page=147}}</ref> The Shadow World also seems to serve as Aebrynis' [[Border Ethereal]].<ref name="gtte16">{{b|Planescape|A Guide to the Ethereal Plane|pdf=17293|page=16}}</ref>
== Personalities ==
The following planar personalities came from Aebrynis:
* The {{NPC|Blowfish|monster|genderless|awnshegh|unclassed|12||ne}}<ref name="poclm33">{{b|Planescape|Planes of Conflict|pdf=17278|page=33, ''Liber Malevolentiae''}}</ref>
== Portals ==
The following portals are known to link to Aebrynis:
* The [[Seafarer's Arch]] in the [[Ditch]] links to a waterfall in Cariele<ref name="poly137-15">{{b|Polyhedron|Polyhedron Magazine 137|page=15}}</ref>
== Gods ==
: See also: [[Cerilian powers]]<ref name="ohg160-164,179">{{b|Planescape|On Hallowed Ground|pdf=121101|nip=1|page=160-164,179}}</ref><ref name="woh9195">{{b|D&D|Warriors of Heaven|pdf=17387|page=91-95}}</ref>
Around [[Prehistory|1398 BFHR]], the gods of the people of ''Cerilia'' sacrificed themselves in one great battle (the Battle of Mount Deismaar) in order to defeat the dark power Azrai. Their closest mortal servants, however, absorbed much of their power, and themselves ascended to godhood. All of Cerilia's current pantheon of gods can trace themselves to this event.
* [[Avani]] (Greater) * [[Erik]] (Greater) * [[Haelyn]] (Greater) * [[Belinik]] (Intermediate) * [[Nesirie]] (Intermediate) * [[Sera]] (Intermediate) * [[Cuiraécen]] (Lesser) * [[Eloéle]] (Lesser) * [[Kriesha]] (Lesser) * [[Laerme]] (Lesser) * [[Ruornil]] (Lesser)
== Background Information ==
'''Aebrynis''' is the primary setting for the ''[[Birthright]]'' campaign setting.

{{Plane | image = | caption = | name = Alfheim | othernames = Elfheim | symbol = Ysgard.png | demonym = | natives = [[Elf|Elves]] | languages = | basicrefs = <ref name="MotP3e-p90-92">{{Cite book/Manual of the Planes 3rd edition|90-92}}</ref><ref name="D236"/><ref name="D41"/> | type-GW = Realm | shape-size-GW = | gravity-GW = Normal | time-GW = Normal | morphic-GW = Divinely | element-energy-GW = Mildly [[Positive energy|positive]]-dominant | alignment-GW = {{Alignment grid|off|off|on|off|off|on|off|off|off}} | magical-GW = Normal | layers-GW = | layer-number-GW = | location-GW = [[Ysgard (layer)|Ysgard]] | refs-GW = <ref name="MotP3e-p90-92" /> | type-WA = | shape-size-WA = | gravity-WA = | mutability-WA = | element-energy-WA = | alignment-WA = | magical-WA = | layers-WA = | layer-number-WA = | location-WA = | refs-WA = | type-WT = | shape-size-WT = | gravity-WT = | time-WT = | morphic-WT = | element-energy-WT = | alignment-WT = | magical-WT = | faith-WT = | layers-WT = | layer-number-WT = | location-WT = | refs-WT = | inhabitants = yes | deities = yes | locations = yes | organizations = | settlements = | usethe = | useon = }} '''Alfheim''', rarely also called '''Elfheim''',<ref name="D236">{{Cite dragon/236/The Seldarine Revisited}}</ref><ref name="D41">{{Cite dragon |issue=41 |title=Giants in the Earth |author=[[Tom Moldvay]] |editor=[[Jake Jaquet]] |date=September 1980 |pages=19}}</ref> was an [[elf|elven]] realm in the [[Ysgard (layer)|first layer]] of [[Ysgard]]. It was occasionally the location of [[Aerie (realm)|Aerie]], the [[divine realm]] of [[Aerdrie Faenya]], according to the [[Great Wheel cosmology]].<ref name="DD2e-p94">{{Cite book/Demihuman Deities|94}}</ref><ref name="OHG2e-p95">{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|95}}</ref>
==Description== The realm was a beautiful and joyful region imbued in sunlight. The landscape was rich with untouched wilds with sunlit forests, streams, and hills, all teeming with wildlife.<ref name="MotP3e-p90-92" /><ref name="PC-BC2e-p109-111">{{Cite book/Planes of Chaos/The Book of Chaos|109-111}}</ref>
Seasons in Alfheim were well defined, with long and mild summers and extremely harsh winters.<ref name="MotP3e-p90-92" />
==Cosmography== Alfheim was believed to have been once part of [[Arvandor]], but the realm gradually shifted into Ysgard as its inhabitants grew increasingly concerned with honor and survival.<ref name="PC-BC2e-p109-111" />
==Notable Locations== * [[Aerie (realm)|Aerie]], the divine realm of [[Aerdrie Faenya]], was occasionally located in Alfheim, as it constantly shifted back and forth from Arvandor.<ref name="DD2e-p94" /><ref name="OHG2e-p95" /> * The [[High Grove]], a copse of enormous [[sequoia]]s that connected to one of the branches of [[Yggdrasil]]. It was the site of large festivals in spring and autumn.<ref name="PC-TL2e-p42,45">{{Cite book/Planes of Chaos/The Travelogue|42,45}}</ref>
==Inhabitants== Most of the elves in Alfheim dwelt on the surface, but it was also common to find settlements located in glittering underground caves. During winter, all surface dwellers retreated to those caves after the first snow. The caves were then sealed off for the duration of the season. Wintertime visitors to Alfheim were met with a deserted landscape devoid of its inhabitants.<ref name="MotP3e-p90-92" /><ref name="PC-BC2e-p109-111" />
During summer, the elven inhabitants of Alfheim were very welcoming to visitors, bestowing them with valuable gifts and insisting for travelers to share tales of their journeys. However, they strongly disliked the [[Ysgardian dwarves]] and [[gnome]]s,<ref name="PC-BC2e-p109-111" /> the former of whom would come up to the surface during this season to farm or engage in trade,<ref name="FB-p124">{{Cite book/Frostburn|124}}</ref> and made every effort to make them feel unwelcome and uncomfortable.<ref name="PC-BC2e-p109-111" />

'''Anhur''' was a Lesser Power of the [[Pharaonic pantheon]]. He shared his portfolio as the Pharaonic god of war with his rival Montju, and they were technically both proxies of the other. Anhur and Montju kept this arrangement to keep an eye on each other in lieu of being able to kill their rival.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book/On Hallowed Ground|86}}</ref>
Anhur ruled the realm of [[Netaph]] on [[Ysgard (layer)|Ysgard]]. His petitioners were fiercely loyal, raiding the [[Hades|Gray Waste]] and [[Abyss]] without the safety net of their god saving them from permanent death.<ref name=":0" />

==Description== Aoskar is described as a "planar power"<ref name="ohg182">{{b|Planescape|On Hallowed Ground|pdf=121101|nip=1|page=182}}</ref>, suggesting that while most powers' worshippers are primarily from a [[Prime Material plane|prime]] world, Aoskar's worshippers were mostly found in the planes.
==Personality== ==Abilities== ==Possessions== ==Divine Realm== ==Activities== ==Relationships== ==History==
At his peak, Aoskar claimed half the planewalkers in Sigil among his worshippers. By all appearances, his power was growing, and he may have stood a chance to claim the entire city. However, the [[Lady of Pain]] did nothing.
It's only when one of her [[dabus]] declared himself a priest of Aoskar that the Lady acted.
The dabus in question was exiled. Shunned by other dabus, barred from official duties, consigned to walk the ground instead of floating above it. Considering him a "fallen" dabus, Cagers named him {{NPC|Fell|proxy|male|dabus|unclassed|7|Sign of One|n}}.<ref name="unc37">{{b|Planescape|Uncaged: Faces of Sigil|pdf=17285|nip=1|page=37}}</ref><ref name="unc112">{{b|Planescape|Uncaged: Faces of Sigil|pdf=17285|nip=1|page=112}}</ref>
Aoskar's temple in Sigil's [[Lower Ward]], the Great Temple of Doors<ref name="unc37">{{b|Planescape|Uncaged: Faces of Sigil|pdf=17285|nip=1|page=37}}</ref><ref name="unc112">{{b|Planescape|Uncaged: Faces of Sigil|pdf=17285|nip=1|page=112}}</ref>, was destroyed, becoming the landmark known to modern Cagers as the [[Shattered Temple]].<ref name="pscs-sab82">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|nip=1|page=82}}, ''Sigil and Beyond''</ref><ref name="pscs-pggtp16">{{b|Planescape|Planescape Campaign Setting|pdf=17267|nip=1|page=16}}, ''A Player's Guide to the Planes''</ref><ref name="fm8">{{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17265|nip=1|page=8}}</ref> Aoskar's image was stricken from the Cage. Aoskar was killed by the Lady, his withered husk consigned to float in the [[Astral Plane]].<ref name="unc37">{{b|Planescape|Uncaged: Faces of Sigil|pdf=17285|nip=1|page=37}}</ref><ref name="unc89">{{b|Planescape|Uncaged: Faces of Sigil|pdf=17285|nip=1|page=89}}</ref><ref name="ohg43">{{b|Planescape|On Hallowed Ground|pdf=121101|nip=1|page=43}}</ref><ref name="gttap38">{{b|Planescape|A Guide to the Astral Plane|pdf=17287|page=38}}</ref><ref name="dttu4">{{b|Planescape|Doors to the Unknown|pdf=17290|nip=1|page=4}}</ref>
The name is rarely uttered, and when it is, it's often used as a curse. The punishment for worshipping Aoskar is death. Although, since Fell was spared by the Lady, most are too afraid of her ire to risk extending the punishment to him.
On the day Aoskar died, [[Four Doors|four portals]] vanished. They reappear for a brief period only once every 500 years, leading some to call them "blinks." No one's sure if the blinks are the Lady's doing or if the portals were Aoskar's dying act, or what the reason either would have to do this in any case.<ref name="dttu4">{{b|Planescape|Doors to the Unknown|pdf=17290|nip=1|page=4}}</ref>
In recent years, the [[Sign of One]] — particularly the [[Will of the One]] subsect — raised [[Aoskar]] as a potential candidate for a god to resurrect through the power of their belief, to convince everyone of the correctness of their philosophy.<ref name="fm125">{{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17265|nip=1|page=125}}</ref><ref name="unc7">{{b|Planescape|Uncaged: Faces of Sigil|pdf=17285|nip=1|page=7}}</ref><ref name="unc37">{{b|Planescape|Uncaged: Faces of Sigil|pdf=17285|nip=1|page=37}}</ref><ref name="unc112">{{b|Planescape|Uncaged: Faces of Sigil|pdf=17285|nip=1|page=112}}</ref><ref name="hbtbw21">{{b|Planescape|Hellbound: The Blood War|pdf=17281|nip=1|page=21}}</ref><ref name="dttu5">{{b|Planescape|Doors to the Unknown|pdf=17290|nip=1|page=5}}</ref><ref name="dttu9">{{b|Planescape|Doors to the Unknown|pdf=17290|nip=1|page=9}}</ref>
==Rumors & Legends== * Some say that Cagers started revering the [[Lady of Pain]] as one of Aoskar's aspects.<ref name="fm124">{{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17265|nip=1|page=124}}</ref> * {{NPC|Wooly Cupgrass|planar|male|bariaur|unclassed|7|Society of Sensation|cn}} is searching for some of Aoskar's blood, having heard a rumor that it functions as a multiversal gate key.<ref name="unc23">{{b|Planescape|Uncaged: Faces of Sigil|pdf=17285|nip=1|page=23}}</ref> * {{NPC|Djhek'nlarr|planar|female|githyanki|fighter|7|class2=mage|level2=4|Free League|le}} sells figurines of Aoskar to [[prime]]s. Though not enough to earn the Lady's ire, it's punishably by two years' hard labor.<ref name="unc25">{{b|Planescape|Uncaged: Faces of Sigil|pdf=17285|nip=1|page=25}}</ref> * Some say that Aoskar will only stay dead as long as there's no god in the Cage. If people start worshipping the Lady — making her a power — Aoskar would be able to return.<ref name="ohg52">{{b|Planescape|On Hallowed Ground|pdf=121101|nip=1|page=52}}</ref>
==Appendix== * Priests of Aoskar had a sacred tongue of their own. In this language, "athaon" meant "godless." ''Athaon'' was later adopted by the [[Athar]] as a term for their [[factotum]]s.<ref name="fm14">{{b|Planescape|The Factol's Manifesto|pdf=17265|nip=1|page=14}}</ref>
